hero.titleLead: A vault for your words that stays
hero.subtitle: Keep notes and credentials with absolute privacy: encrypted on your device, no cloud, no account, no compromise.

features.title: Built for Privacy
features.subtitle: Every layer is designed so your data never leaves the device.

items.title: Zero-Knowledge
items.body: AES-GCM 256-bit encryption happens on your device, before data touches storage. No server can read it.

items.title: Keys on Device
items.body: Keys are derived with Argon2id plus a random salt, then live only in memory while the session is open. They are never sent or stored on a server.

items.title: Offline-First
items.body: Data lives in IndexedDB or a local file. No internet, no account, no forced sync. The vault still opens.

items.title: Panic Key
items.body: One emergency passphrase permanently wipes the entire vault. A kill switch that works even when you have no time to think.

items.title: CLI · TUI · Web
items.body: Terminal for automation and remote servers, TUI for comfort, web dashboard for visuals. All on one vault.

items.title: Open Source (MIT)
items.body: The entire codebase is open and auditable. Privacy claims should be provable, not just trusted.

security.title: An architecture you can audit
security.subtitle: No magic and no black boxes. These four steps are the entire journey of your data, and all of it happens on this device.
guarantees: No telemetry, analytics, or network requests.
No account, no email, no cloud storing your data.
The session key can be cleared from memory whenever you want.
Panic key wipes the vault instantly in an emergency.
MIT. You can audit the source yourself on GitHub.

pipeline.title: Password + random salt
pipeline.note: Argon2id (memory-hard, 64 MiB) processes your passphrase on device. The result never leaves this machine.

pipeline.title: AES-GCM 256-bit
pipeline.note: Every entry is encrypted with a unique 12-byte IV, so data patterns never leak through ciphertext.

pipeline.title: SHA-256 integrity
pipeline.note: Every entry carries a verification hash, and the audit trail is hash-chained, so silent changes are detected.

pipeline.title: Local storage
pipeline.note: The browser uses IndexedDB; the CLI stores a JSON file with 0o600 permissions inside a 0o700 directory.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subtitle: The things people ask the most.

items.q: Is my data sent to a server?
items.a: No. Lembaranz runs entirely on your device. The browser uses IndexedDB, the CLI uses local files, and no backend ever receives your vault contents.

items.q: What happens if I forget my master password?
items.a: The key cannot be recovered from a server, because no server holds it. Keep the recovery mnemonic generated during setup in a safe place. Without it, the data cannot be opened.

items.q: Can I use it without internet?
items.a: Yes. Once the page has loaded, the entire vault works fully offline. No network requests are made while you read or write.

items.q: Do I have to install anything to try it?
items.a: No. Open the dashboard straight in your browser. The CLI is optional, for automation and terminal users who want the vault stored as a local file.
Yes. MIT licensed, free, and self-hostable. No paid tiers, no entry limits.
